previous_disclosures.section: Termination of the Arm Share Purchase Agreement
previous_disclosures.summary: NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the Share Purchase Agreement for the acquisition of Arm in February 2022 due to significant regulatory challenges, resulting in a $1.35 billion acquisition termination cost recorded in fiscal year 2023.

Operating expenses increased 50% year-over-year to include a $1.35 billion acquisition termination charge for the Arm transaction, alongside increased compensation, data center infrastructure, and engineering development costs.
NVIDIA recorded an acquisition termination cost of $1.35 billion in fiscal year 2023 related to the Arm transaction, reflecting the write-off of the prepayment provided at signing.

Cash provided by operating activities decreased in fiscal year 2023 compared to 2022, primarily due to a decrease in net income adjusted for non-cash items (including a $1.35 billion Arm acquisition termination cost) and higher tax payments, partially offset by changes in working capital driven by lower accounts receivable.

comparisons.peer_topic: All Other operating loss breakdown for 2024 and 2023
comparisons.peer_summary: All Other operating loss was $4.2 billion in 2024 and $4.4 billion in 2023, primarily consisting of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and stock-based compensation expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD report on the variance and composition of their 'All Other' operating segments. A key similarity is that stock-based compensation expense is a primary driver for the 'All Other' loss in both companies, with NVIDIA attributing an $839 million year-over-year increase in fiscal 2024 and AMD reporting $1.4 billion in stock-based compensation for both fiscal 2024 and 2023. The key difference is the magnitude and nature of other costs: AMD's 'All Other' loss is heavily dominated by amortization of acquisition-related intangibles ($2.4 billion in 2024), which NVIDIA does not highlight as a primary component of its 'All Other' variance in the same disclosure context, whereas NVIDIA explicitly references a one-time $1.4 billion Arm acquisition termination cost in the prior fiscal year (2023) as a major factor in the year-over-year decrease in its loss.
